pr_title: PromQL: Fix string and parentheses handling in engine
pr_body:
Will fix #6610.

There are still problems at the font end side.

The old UI handles string returns on queries like `"foo"` or `("bar")` just fine, however the react UI claims the return type is a scalar.

Could someone who is more familiar with the React UI look into this, maybe @juliusv or @boyskila ?

Signed-off-by: Tobias Guggenmos <tguggenm@redhat.com>

pr_comments:
Can you please add tests?

```diff
diff --git a/promql/testdata/aggregators.test b/promql/testdata/aggregators.test
index 0da80576..7b3ba45b 100644
--- a/promql/testdata/aggregators.test
+++ b/promql/testdata/aggregators.test
@@ -233,6 +233,11 @@ eval instant at 5m count_values("version", version)
 	{version="7"} 2
 	{version="8"} 2
 
+eval instant at 5m count_values(((("version"))), version)
+	{version="6"} 5
+	{version="7"} 2
+	{version="8"} 2
+
 eval instant at 5m count_values without (instance)("version", version)
 	{job="api-server", group="production", version="6"} 3
 	{job="api-server", group="canary", version="8"} 2
```

```
    promql_test.go:32: unexpected error: error evaluating query "count_values((((\"version\"))), version)" (line 236): unexpected error: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
```

Thanks!

So I guess we should get to consensus about how to deal with these parentheses in #6598 first, i.e. figure out whether we should fix that kind of bug in the engine or let it already fail during parse time.

> The old UI handles string returns on queries like "foo" or ("bar") just fine, however the react UI claims the return type is a scalar.
>
> Could someone who is more familiar with the React UI look into this, maybe @juliusv or @boyskila ?

I think it's just a typo in the string handling case: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8cb2ab6a9913d7735c729a03964bf485053aca35/web/ui/react-app/src/DataTable.tsx#L106

Ironically we already even support strings as a root-level type in the UI (except for this typo), probably because the new UI code was partially adapted from the old UI code, and 1.x Prometheus once supported root-level strings already.

> 1.x Prometheus once supported root-level strings already.

I don't think we ever did, though some of the code that'd be needed to support it was there.
Can we please have negative tests? rate((foo)[5m]).
Still working on another PR, this one will come after.
This PR now (hopefully) fixes #6598, fixes #6610  and is ready for review.

issue_context.title: PromQL: Allow engine to return strings
issue_context.body:
## Problem
`promql.ParseExpr` will parse expressions of all types without syntax errors, but the engine can only evaluate expressions of type `vector` and `matrix`.

## Proposal

Add a `ParseQuery` func that will behave like `ParseExpr` but will panic if the type of the AST root has a type that can not be evaluated by the engine, i.e. is a scalar or string.

This would also solve part of the problem pointed out in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/6598#issuecomment-573624531.
comments: Scalar should and strings could be fine. String is a valid promql type.

For reference, the current error for a root expression like `"foo"` happens here: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8cb2ab6a9913d7735c729a03964bf485053aca35/promql/engine.go#L1322

Wouldn't it be better to fix the engine to support evaluating any of the four value types as the root node, rather than adding such a new function?

Does anyone want to work on a PR for that?

Otherwise I can do it.

Either is fine, feel free to go ahead.

I hope it won't create too many complications. E.g. range evals for strings wouldn't work, I guess.

> E.g. range evals for strings wouldn't work, I guess.

That should already be caught by the parser.

This issue is only about the case of the root node being a string.

Yes, but root nodes can be evaluated at an instant or over a range (graph), but matrix root nodes already can't be evaluated over a range, only scalars and vectors can. So I guess strings would have the same restrictions as matrix nodes.

review_comments:
I'd prefer not to mutate the main (non-cache etc.) fields of the AST during the query. E.g. a user might want to serialize or otherwise use it again after executing.

Could we make this functional?

```suggestion
		param := unwrapParenExpr(&e.Param)
```

I agree that functional execution would be nicer.

However, evaluation already mutates the AST in other places, so actually making this functional would be a larger effort.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/master/promql/engine.go#L1056
Re-evaluation might still produce correct results, but I wouldn't rely on it.
Damn. My worst fears are confirmed ;) I think in this case it'd be really easy to avoid a mutation though, and fewer mutations cause fewer confusions.

I quickly skimmed the code and found a couple places where evaluation has side effects on (non-cache) AST contents.

All of them look relatively fixable.

If functional execution is desired, I'd prefer to fix all of them in a separate PR and leave this one as is.
Ok, I'd say let's put that on hold for now then and keep things as is here.
I've made an issue for this #6627
